correctness.rationale: The first-index obstruction excludes all offdiagonal cells; comparing products with each matrix-unit singleton forces a common conjugacy-invariant diagonal fiber. Conversely these and only these subsets commute with every singleton, hence with every nonempty subset. Diagonal set products produce zero iff n>=2 or one factor already contains zero. Finite group subsets H with H^2=H are exactly subgroups, and conjugation stability means normality. Exhaustive eight-case checks match the resulting full center and idempotents. Finite experiments do not prove the all-group theorem.

value.rationale: A uniform complete classification for all finite groups, not a single small example: its center size recovers the number of conjugacy classes; its central idempotent count recovers the number of normal subgroups; and exact multiplication distinguishes the one-index and multiple-index Brandt regimes despite constant cardinality. These are intrinsic, group-theoretic invariants of a natural power-semigroup construction motivating current inverse-semigroup rigidity research.
